cards.title: What is a conditional?
cards.body: Conditionals are if-sentences: one part is the condition (if…), the other is the result. English uses different tenses to show how real or imaginary the situation is.
cards.body_cz: Kondicionály jsou věty s if: jedna část je podmínka (if…), druhá je výsledek. Angličtina volí časy podle toho, jak reálná nebo hypotetická situace je.
points: If it rains, I stay home. (condition → result)
Order can flip: I stay home if it rains.
The tense pattern tells you: fact · real future · unreal now

cards.title: Three useful types (overview)
cards.body: You already met zero and first (A2). This pack is the second conditional. Keep the three jobs separate:
cards.body_cz: Zero a first už znáš z A2. Tento balíček je second conditional. Drž tři funkce odděleně:

cards.title: Zero conditional (reminder)
cards.body: When something is always or usually true — science, rules, habits. Both clauses stay in the present.
cards.body_cz: Když něco platí vždy / obvykle — fakta, pravidla, zvyky. Obě části v přítomném čase.
points: If you heat ice, it melts.
If I am tired, I go to bed early.
Not: If you will heat ice…

cards.title: First conditional (reminder)
cards.body: Real future possibility: this might actually happen. If-clause = present; result = will + base.
cards.body_cz: Reálná budoucí možnost: může se opravdu stát. If = přítomný čas; výsledek = will + base.
points: If it rains tomorrow, I will stay home.
If you study, you will pass.
Not: If it will rain… · Not: If it rained, I will… (mixed by mistake)

cards.title: Second conditional (this pack)
cards.body: Imaginary, unlikely, or contrary-to-now situations. English uses past forms in the if-clause — but the meaning is about now / future, not a finished past story.
cards.body_cz: Hypotetické, nepravděpodobné nebo „teď to tak není“. V if je minulý tvar — ale význam je o teď / budoucnosti, ne o hotovém minulém příběhu.
points: would + base (travel, not travels / to travel)
Past in if = distance from reality, not “yesterday story”

cards.title: Compare the same idea
cards.body: Same topic, different stance — choose the pattern that matches how real it is:
cards.body_cz: Stejné téma, jiný postoj — zvol vzorec podle toho, jak reálné to je:

table.caption: rain · stay home
rows: If it rains, I stay home.
If it rains tomorrow, I will stay home.
If it rained tomorrow, I would stay home.

points: First: will · Second: would
First if-clause: rains (present) · Second if-clause: rained (past form)

cards.title: were
cards.body: In second conditional, were is common for all persons in careful English — especially advice: If I were you…
cards.body_cz: Ve second conditional je were běžné pro všechny osoby — hlavně rada: If I were you…
points: If I were rich… (also heard: If I was… — learn were first)
If she were free, she would join us.

cards.title: Questions
cards.body: Put would first in the result question; the if-clause still uses past.
cards.body_cz: V otázce dej would dopředu; if-věta pořád s minulým tvarem.
points: Would you move if they offered you the job?
What would you do if you lost your phone?

cards.title: What you practise
cards.body: Gaps may sit on would, on the past verb in the if-clause, or on were. Read the whole sentence before you choose.
cards.body_cz: Mezera může být na would, na minulém slovese v if, nebo na were. Nejdřív přečti celou větu.
points: If I ____ more time, I would travel. → had
If I had more time, I ____ travel. → would
If I ____ you, I would call. → were
